{{Short description|Summation method for some divergent series}}
{{Use American English|date = March 2019}}
{{Use mdy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=June 2024}}
{{CS1 config|mode=cs2}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Euler–Boole summation''' is a method for summing [[alternating series]]. The concept is named after [[Leonhard Euler]] and [[George Boole]]. Boole published this summation method, using [[Euler's polynomials]], but the method itself was likely already known to Euler.{{r|bcm|temme}}

Euler's polynomials are defined by{{r|bcm}}
{{bi|left=1.6|<math>\displaystyle\frac{2e^{xt}}{e^t+1}=\sum_{n=0}^\infty E_n(x)\frac{t^n}{n!}.</math>}}
The periodic Euler functions modify these by a sign change depending on the parity of the integer part of <math>x</math>:{{r|bcm}}
{{bi|left=1.6|<math>\displaystyle\widetilde E_n(x+1)=-\widetilde E_n(x)\text{ and } \widetilde E_n(x)=E_n(x) \text{ for } 0<x<1.</math>}}

The Euler–Boole formula to sum alternating series is
{{bi|left=1.6|<math>
\begin{align}
\displaystyle\sum_{j=a}^{n-1}(-1)^j f(j+h) = {}&\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=0}^{m-1} \frac{E_k(h)}{k!} \left((-1)^{n-1} f^{(k)}(n)+(-1)^a f^{(k)}(a)\right)\\
&{}+ \frac 1 {2(m-1)!} \int_a^n f^{(m)}(x)\widetilde E_{m-1}(h-x) \, dx,
\end{align}</math>}}
where <math>a,m,n\in\N, a<n, h\in [0,1]</math> and <math>f^{(k)}</math> is the ''k''th [[derivative]].{{r|bcm|temme}}
